title: NC-Bench and NCfold: A Benchmark and Closed-Loop Framework for RNA Non-Canonical Base-Pair Prediction
claim: Embeddings from different pretrained models differ sharply in isotropy, with one model far more isotropic than the others.
layout: single panel, seven violin plots left-to-right, colored by model
description: A single violin plot compares IsoScore distributions, on the y-axis from 0 to about 0.18, across seven RNA foundation models. The models are RNA-FM, UTRLM, SpliceBERT, structRFM, RNAErnie, RiNALMo and AIDO.RNA, listed along the x-axis with rotated labels. Each violin has its own color: blue, green, orange, red, light blue and pink. Inner black bars show the interquartile range, with a white median tick. UTRLM, in green, dominates the plot. It is tall and wide, with a median near 0.105. The other models are compressed near zero. RNAErnie and AIDO.RNA are nearly flat slivers. Dashed horizontal gridlines help read values. The eye goes first to the tall green violin.
caption: IsoScore distributions of RFMs.
abstract: RNA secondary structure forms the basis for folding and function, with non-canonical (NC) interactions indispensable for catalysis, regulation, and molecular recognition. Despite their importance, predicting NC base pairs remains challenging due to the absence of a standardized benchmark for systematic evaluation. To address this, we introduce NC-Bench, the first benchmark dedicated to NC base-pair prediction. NC-Bench provides 925 curated RNA sequences with 6,708 high-quality NC annotations, fine-grained edge and orientation classification tasks, and IsoScore-based embedding evaluation, offering a rigorous foundation for systematic assessment. Building on this, we propose NCfold, a dual-branch framework that couples sequence features with structural priors derived from RNA foundation models (RFMs) via Representative Embedding Fusion (REF) and REF-weighted self-attention. The closed-loop design iteratively refines sequence and structure representations, alleviating data sparsity and enhancing predictive accuracy. Experiments on NC-Bench show that NCfold outperforms existing methods, with zero-shot and ablation studies confirming its effectiveness and underscoring the need for NC-specific benchmarks. Together, NC-Bench and NCfold establish a systematic foundation for NC base-pair prediction, advancing our understanding of RNA structure and enabling next-generation RNA-centric applications. The datasets and codes are publicly available at https://github.com/heqin-zhu/NCBench.
